method.transport: GitHub GraphQL and REST through authenticated gh API; primary issue, PR, comment, review, commit, and file records only
method.classification: The 147-item union preserves every exact search hit. The 88-item direct set selects titles explicitly about ANE, Neural Engine, ANE prefill, or Qwen prefill. Tangential matches remain in thread_inventory.
limitations: GitHub search is lexical and can include a thread only because an ANE term appears in a comment.
No issue or PR exceeded the 100-comment page fetched; the maximum was 44.
No formal PR reviews or inline review comments existed in the fetched corpus; PR conversation was in issue-style discussion comments.
PR #3118 had more than 100 commits/files, but it was tangential and its discussion was complete.
No Apple device or ANE runtime was used in this research run.

priority_threads.finding: A proposal for GPU decode plus background ANE prefill and KV warmup. It contains no implementation, benchmark, hardware result, or compatibility proof. Its only comment links ANEMLL.
priority_threads.actionable_read: Treat same-model branch warmup as the first bounded experiment. Cross-model KV reuse needs an explicit compatibility proof and must not be assumed from unified memory.

priority_threads.finding: oMLX 0.6.2 accepted ANE enabled on an oQ8e checkpoint while the then-current gate/up eligibility was 4-bit, produced no INFO/WARNING signal, and exposed no API status. The reporter observed a 3.0 s load versus a claimed 27–29 s ANE eager-compile signal; that timing was an indirect diagnosis, not an ANE measurement.

resolution.change: Warnings for dispatch/no-eligible/zero-compiled exits plus an /api/status ane_prefill block.

priority_threads.remaining_caveat: The maintainer noted at merge that VLM engines used _vlm_model and were skipped by the status aggregation, and that available meant patch importability rather than hardware availability.

observed_contracts: CoreML conversion and inference pipeline rather than oMLX private-runtime procedure banks
coremltools>=9.0, Xcode Command Line Tools/CoreML compiler, Python 3.9-3.11
Apple Neural Engine FP16 range is ±65,504; ANEMLL ships FP16 preflight/scaling guidance
M1/A14 non-uniform state-shape restriction is documented for Gemma 3 monolithic models
README says LUT4 quality remains weak without block quantization

findings.status: merged implementation plus measured community data
findings.finding: The foundational path compiles one exact flattened token count, normally 2,048. Wider inputs can tile onto that shape; tails need GPU fallback or local intermediate padding. The delivered scheduler chunk must be at least the compiled ANE tile or the bank compiles and never dispatches.
details: #2890 hardware-checked 4,096 rows as two 2,048 tiles and 4,608 rows as two tiles plus a 512-row tail on M3 Ultra.
#2966 pads only intermediate MLP/GDN activation rows, slices before recurrence or later layers, and derives the profitable tail threshold as floor(S*G/H)+1.
Synthetic prompt tokens are not safe padding because they change positions, KV, logits, and recurrent state.

findings.status: merged implementation; measured on M3 Ultra
findings.finding: oMLX packs 64 MLP plus 48 GDN procedures into two instance-pinned programs because the private runtime accepted about 121 resident handles in testing. One program per layer would exhaust that budget.
details: The combined 112-procedure bank was reported to take about 37–44 s to compile on the reference M3 Ultra.
A single unpinned 55% MLP slice measured 57.90 ms versus 41.51 ms for two instance-pinned calls.
This is a report from one hardware/configuration, not a portable H13 constant.

findings.finding: The shipped oMLX path requantizes selected source weights to per-output-channel INT8 for ANE. Q5, affine Q6, and affine Q8 support landed, while BF16 checkpoint support remains an open request for mixed BF16 GPU plus FP16 ANE execution.
details: #2833 supports Q6 GDN at affine group sizes 64 and 128 and keeps Q8 GDN b/a projections on stock MLX because packed Q8 failed recurrent-state accuracy checks.
#2889 maintainer hardware parity on M3 Ultra reported q5 gate/up at gs64 and gs128, single and dual ANE, cosine >=0.999979 against stock MLX.
#3104 asks to keep the checkpoint BF16, make selected ANE weights FP16, and explicitly convert/merge BF16↔FP16; no implementation is linked.

findings.finding: Approximate INT8 errors cannot be allowed into recurrence just because per-layer cosine looks good. #3133 caps GDN ANE work at 6,144 token-local z rows and leaves all 10,240 recurrent qkv rows on checkpoint-precision GPU, making the effective ceiling 37.5%.
details: The PR attributes deterministic 32K failures to recurrent qkv rows on the INT8 path.
M3 Ultra validation reported recurrent-safe prefill at 588.2 tok/s for 4K and 503.0 tok/s for 32K versus 465.8 and 410.1 GPU-only, without decode-speed regression.
A NAX tester still found run-to-run variance for restore-at-2K-boundary then ANE-prefill; answers stayed correct. This remains a regression shape worth preserving.

findings.finding: A universal split is contradicted by M1/M2 results. The same tuner and model produced different winners by part and topology.

measurements.caveat: Reporter says cross-part absolute PP is not comparable because residency and thermal state differed; within-part ratios are the signal.
Pre-rebase branch results; M2 baseline changed after memory-guard adjustment.

rows.result: Full-model ANE prefill was 0.83x GPU-only for a 2,259-token prompt; q6 GDN microbench up to 1.492x but q8 shared expert 0.533–0.791x.
Full-model tuner median 457.4→472.5 tok/s (+3.30%); repeated run +3.37%; q4/q5/q6 GDN microbench 1.3562–1.4735x and q8 shared expert 1.0968–1.2513x.

measurements.caveat: PR #3298 was closed unmerged as superseded.

findings.status: merged fixes plus one open draft
findings.finding: No searched oMLX issue or PR mentions SRAM. The actionable evidence concerns resident compiled banks, FP16 IOSurfaces, Metal headroom, and kernel neural-ledger memory; do not relabel these as SRAM.
details: #2933 reserves per-slice FP16 input/output IOSurfaces as (input_dim + ane_output) * sequence_length * 2, doubled for dual-ANE slices, and explicitly calls this a floor because merge scratch is omitted.
#3364 finds the VLM scheduler snapshots this reserve before ANE bank compilation and adds an after-compile refresh.
#3103 measured about 13 GB of mapped bank blobs for a 27B mlp0.35/gdn0.45 configuration and adds bank shedding under recurring prefill pressure.
#3425 is open/draft. It claims a default Qwen3.8-27B compiled bank size of 7.06 GB and proposes pricing from compiled file size because phys_footprint/MLX accounting cannot see the neural ledger.

findings.finding: Compilation must be incremental, bounded, cache-keyed by environment, and able to fail open. Blind split retries can stack asynchronous driver cleanup and trigger jetsam.
details: A maintainer comment reports incremental staging reduced a 27B bank compile spike from 36 GB to 4.7 GB.
#2999 checks phys_footprint against 70% of total memory before each retry, forces GC, and allows driver cleanup to settle.
#2975 warm compile-cache hits reduced fresh-process load time by 53–66% on M1 Ultra, M2 Max, and M1 Max, with stable identifiers keyed by OS build, ANE identifier, instance, and MIL.
#3124 traced macOS 27 Code=10 to setModelURL on _ANEInMemoryModel; commit 7d77098 removed that caller-assigned URL while retaining content-hash reuse.

findings.finding: ANE/GPU concurrency needs explicit completion ordering, bounded waits, and permanent per-module fallbacks. More asynchrony was not automatically faster.
details: #2756 reports Metal-callback ANE submission increased a representative layer from about 47.5 ms to 71 ms; the blocking input-pack wait was retained.
Commit b9d3a191 waits for the GPU suffix before hybrid merge.
#3002 bounds every ANE evaluation wait and latches timed-out programs.
#3105 rolls single/dual dispatch back on mid-flight exceptions.
#3123 routes full tiles to GPU when active Metal memory exceeds 85% of effective wired cap and fixes missing latch checks.

findings.status: measured issue evidence; unresolved scheduler gap
findings.finding: ANE can mitigate GPU contention but does not solve continuous-batching fairness. Shadow prefill competes with active decode unless admission and fair-share policy are explicit.
details: #2795 reports batch 1/2/4/8 decode throughput 42.3/43.0/89.7/157.1 tok/s with ANE on, while prefill throughput fell 212.4→131.2 tok/s.

#3209 reports a short request retaining only 13–24% of solo decode throughput during a concurrent 60K prefill on M3 Ultra. ANE improved the contended Qwen decoder from 8.9 to 14.7 tok/s, but retention remained 23.4%.
#1107 has no scheduler implementation or measurement, so it does not establish that background warmup is free.

findings.finding: Eligibility must encode architecture, dtype, group size, rank, dimensions, tile, scheduler width, OS/runtime ABI, and instance count. Unsupported work must fall back with a named reason.
details: Dense Qwen MLP was the initial target. Routed MoE rank-3 experts remain GPU-side; #3156 is open and proposes refusing ANE prefill for MoE models.
#3116 shows a tuner selecting fused_down on single-ANE gs64 although the path required dual ANE plus dense Q4 gs128.
#3434 reports NAX variant 6 wrong by max absolute error 5–8 at all tested q4/q8 gs64/gs128 shapes; the open PR removes it and keeps variant 0 default.
#3298 limited experimental Qwen4 to stable dense shared-expert and GDN input projections, excluded routed experts and MTP-only layers, and was later closed as superseded.

findings.finding: oMLX ANE support is not just a compiler artifact: it depends on private AppleNeuralEngine runtime symbols, native custom kernels, Metal toolchain output, matching nanobind/MLX ABI, and correct wheel installation.
details: OMLX_WITH_CUSTOM_KERNEL=1 source builds need the separately downloadable Xcode Metal toolchain component.
A reported nanobind 2.15.0 build imported as ABI-incompatible with MLX; pinned nanobind 2.13.0 worked in that environment.
uv wheel-cache reuse can install a kernel-less wheel after successfully compiling extensions; --no-cache fixed the reported case.
M2 Ultra #3044 had the private runtime probe unavailable; #3067 changed tuner behavior to a completed GPU-only result instead of unloading the model.

findings.finding: Compilation success, dispatch execution, and hardware availability are different states and must be reported separately. A configured flag is not proof that ANE executed.
details: #2829 rejects tuner rankings when no ANE operation was observed.
#2904 adds attempted/configured/layer/program counters and warnings.
The API needs engine-specific model lookup and a field whose name distinguishes patch importability from hardware/runtime availability.

implementable_opportunities.name: Generalize H13 from matvec to fixed-row FP16 linear tiles
implementable_opportunities.why: The local H13 compiler at 28129e4 accepts only fp16 x[1,K], K=256 or 512, constant weights producing [1,512]. oMLX evidence says useful prefill begins with exact fixed-row projection tiles and wider-input tiling.
minimum_change: Keep N=512 and K in {256,512} for the first hardware-qualified step.
Add compile-time M>1 input/output layouts and encode repeated fixed-row work without adding dynamic shapes.
Name unsupported M/alignment/dtype errors; do not silently lower to a different shape.
acceptance_proof: On H13 hardware, compare M-row output against CPU fp16 reference over valid finite inputs.
Verify M=tile, 2*tile, and tile+tail dispatch; the compiler artifact itself remains exact-shape.
Record task/constants/allocation bytes and actual ANE execution, not only successful package creation.

implementable_opportunities.name: Make eligibility and execution provenance first-class manifest data
implementable_opportunities.why: #2824 and #2828 show that configuration, compilation, and execution can disagree silently.
minimum_change: Extend the H13 manifest with requested_shape, compiled_shape, dtype, operation, eligible boolean, and a stable named ineligibility reason.
At runtime expose attempted, compiled, executed, fallback_reason, and observed operation counts.
Keep compile errors named; never map runtime unavailable, missing extension, unsupported shape, and zero execution to one message.
acceptance_proof: A supported matvec reports compiled and executed.
Each unsupported dtype/shape/transpose reports its distinct existing or new error contract.
A deliberately unavailable runtime reports fallback without claiming execution.

implementable_opportunities.name: Emit exact persistent and transient memory metadata
implementable_opportunities.why: The H13 package already knows task bytes, constant bytes, tensor allocation bytes, and shapes. oMLX repeatedly failed when bank and IOSurface costs were absent or snapshotted before compile.
minimum_change: Add per-program constant/task bytes and input/output allocation totals to a stable accounting block.
For a runtime bank, sum compiled artifacts separately from per-request input/output surfaces and temporary merge buffers.
Refresh the live reservation after compile and clear it when programs are released.
acceptance_proof: Manifest totals equal emitted file sections and TensorLayout allocationBytes.
A multi-program aggregate equals the sum of its members without double counting shared constants.
After release, runtime reservation returns to zero and provenance records the release.

implementable_opportunities.name: Add procedure-bank packaging before full Qwen graph lowering
implementable_opportunities.why: oMLX needed 112 layer-specific procedures but only two resident program handles; the local H13 package currently emits exactly one operation/program.
minimum_change: Define a package index that contains multiple independently addressable H13 programs and layer-specific constants.
Do not add multi-operation fusion yet; preserve one qualified operation per procedure.
Hash target generation, program bytes, constants, shape, and instance affinity for stable cache identity.
acceptance_proof: Load and execute at least two procedures with different constants from one package.
Prove unload releases every program and a warm reload reuses only an exact hash match.
Reject an OS/target/shape hash mismatch rather than using a stale compiled artifact.

implementable_opportunities.name: Implement local activation-tail padding as a runtime transform
implementable_opportunities.why: It recovers near-full residual tiles without pretending the compiler supports dynamic shapes or adding learned padding tokens.
minimum_change: Zero-pad only the MLP/linear activation to the compiled row count.
Slice outputs back before KV, RoPE, recurrence, or any stateful operation.
Persist a calibrated minimum tail row threshold; below it use GPU/CPU fallback.
acceptance_proof: Real rows match unpadded execution within the chosen FP16 tolerance.
Rows added for padding never reach downstream state.
Threshold boundary selects fallback at threshold-1 and ANE at threshold.

implementable_opportunities.name: Build a bounded compile and cache lifecycle
implementable_opportunities.why: Source-native compilation is only useful in serving if failed retries cannot exhaust memory and valid artifacts can be reused safely.
minimum_change: Stage and release one weight slice at a time.
Before retries, measure the ledger that governs process termination; bound retries and settle asynchronous teardown.
Cache by exact target/OS/compiler/program/constant/shape identity with bounded locking and fail-open temporary compilation.
acceptance_proof: Injected compile failure cannot produce an unbounded retry or leave a live program.
Two concurrent compiles of one key yield one writer and one bounded waiter.
A bad cache hit is purged once, recompiled once, and either executes or returns a named failure.

implementable_opportunities.name: Add INT8 lowering only after fixed-row FP16 is hardware-qualified
implementable_opportunities.why: oMLX gains come from per-output-channel INT8 ANE weights, but long-context and recurrent-state reports show that local parity is insufficient.
minimum_change: Start with affine per-output-channel INT8 constants for stateless dense linear only.
Keep recurrent qkv, attention state, and dynamic MoE routing outside the approximate path.
Preserve original FP16/quantized weights for exact fallback.
acceptance_proof: Finite-value range checks before conversion; reject NaN/Inf and FP16 overflow.
Layer output, final logits, top token, and long-context task probes against FP16 baseline.
Include prefix-restore-at-tile-boundary then re-prefill, with MTP/speculation disabled for determinism.

implementable_opportunities.name: Lower fused gated MLP by hidden-channel partition
implementable_opportunities.why: #2935 shows the mathematically sound fused topology: each ANE/GPU/CPU branch computes gate, up, SwiGLU, and the matching down-weight columns, then full-width partial outputs are summed.
minimum_change: Require multi-operation H13 scheduling and qualified SwiGLU before attempting this.
Partition hidden channels, never final output rows.
Gate on exact dtype, group size, dimensions, instance count, and tile availability; fall back per projection.
acceptance_proof: Full-width sum matches unfused FP16 reference within tolerance and contains no NaN/Inf.
Single and dual-instance paths are separately qualified.
Full-model or representative multi-layer benchmark must beat unfused execution on the target; do not hardcode a split from another SoC.

implementable_opportunities.name: Prototype same-model shadow prefill with strict admission
implementable_opportunities.why: #1107 identifies a real agentic latency pattern, but #3209 shows background prefill can destroy active decode fairness.
minimum_change: Limit the first prototype to the same model, tokenizer, weights, cache format, and exact prompt prefix.
Use idle-only admission with a cancellable queue and a hard memory reservation.
Do not claim cross-model KV interoperability; keep warmed caches isolated by model identity and compiler/program hash.
acceptance_proof: Active decode throughput and latency stay within an explicit measured budget during background work.
Cancellation releases buffers/program references and cannot leave a worker spinning.
A cache is consumed only by the exact compatible model/program identity.
